dimensions.assessment: Affects private sector and government employers who conduct self-audits and employees who receive back wages or settle claims under the program.
dimensions.evidence: allows employers to self-report federal minimum wage and overtime compensation violations as an alternative to litigation

dimensions.assessment: Provides a formal alternative settlement process where employers pay back wages for unintentional violations, and employees who accept settlements waive private rights of action for those claims.
dimensions.evidence: acceptance by an affected employee of an offer of settlement... shall... constitute a waiver... of a private right of action

dimensions.assessment: Prohibits the Administrator from requiring payment to participate, but involves the payment of back wages by employers to employees under supervised settlements without stating federal budget totals.
dimensions.evidence: pay such employee the full amount of unpaid minimum wages or overtime compensation

dimensions.assessment: Creates a permanent statutory program within the Department of Labor's Wage and Hour Division and amends the Fair Labor Standards Act.
dimensions.evidence: The Administrator shall establish a Payroll Audit Independent Determination program

dimensions.assessment: Establishes an ongoing, permanent Department of Labor program for resolving wage and hour violations.
dimensions.evidence: To establish the Payroll Audit Independent Determination program in the Department of Labor.

missing_information: Estimated administrative costs for the Department of Labor to oversee the program
Total projected volume of participating employers and back-wage disbursements
importance_detail.rationale: Establishes a statutory Payroll Audit Independent Determination program in the Department of Labor, allowing employers to self-report and remedy minimum wage and overtime violations under supervision, waiving private rights of action for participating employees upon full payment.
